messages.author: e5d57163f1ae749d
messages.subject: geom_raster giving strange error??
parts:
Hi All,

I am having some difficultly running some code to make a plot of predictions using geom_raster() and was hoping someone might be able to help. All of my code seemed to be working just last week and now I am not sure what I did, but it appears something that I did has created a problem in the code where an attempt to plot the predictions causes the following error: Error in t.default(x) : long vectors not supported yet: ../../../../R-3.2.4/src/main/memory.c:1648. Notably, if I change the plot theme to geom_point everything seems to work fine.

I have attached an example datafile and code snippet below that has been generating the error. I am running R (Version 3.2.4, Platform x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 64 bit) on a MacBook Air and using ggplot2 2.1.0:

sessionInfo(package = "ggplot2")
R version 3.2.4 (2016-03-10)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 (64-bit)
Running under: OS X 10.10.2 (Yosemite)

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
character(0)

other attached packages:
[1] ggplot2_2.1.0

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] colorspace_1.2-6 scales_0.4.0     plyr_1.8.3       graphics_3.2.4   tools_3.2.4      gtable_0.2.0    
 [7] utils_3.2.4      grDevices_3.2.4  Rcpp_0.12.3      stats_3.2.4      datasets_3.2.4   grid_3.2.4      
[13] methods_3.2.4    munsell_0.4.3    base_3.2.4      

Thanks in advance!

Sincerely,

Andrew


################### Code start
library(ggplot2)

pred.df<- read.csv("~/Desktop/predictions.example.csv")

ggplot(data = pred.df, aes(x = long, y = lat, fill = pred)) + 
  geom_raster(interpolate = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(name = "P (Pres)", colours = c("white", "#ffffb2", "#fecc5c", "#fd8d3c", "#e31a1c"), na.value = "steelblue", breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 1, by = 0.25), limits = c(0,1))

################## End

messages.author: e5d57163f1ae749d
messages.subject: Re: geom_raster giving strange error??
parts:
As usual, user error. A corrupted prediction file, where the resulting file was no longer a rectangular grid, appearing to cause the geom_raster() issues.

- Andrew
